name: L-lysine
short: In reviews of 71 studies (12 relatively high quality), adverse events were mainly gut symptoms, with no significant rise in their risk. Data on excess intake are limited; it may unbalance amino acids.
text: A systematic review of 71 intervention studies of L-lysine taken by mouth, with 3357 participants and dosing periods of 1 to 1095 days, found that the observed adverse events were mainly subjective gastrointestinal symptoms; the pooled risk of gastrointestinal symptoms was not significantly increased (risk ratio 1.02), and the authors set a provisional no-observed-adverse-effect level in healthy people at 6.0 g a day, based on those symptoms. The background of that abstract states that safety information on excessive L-lysine intake is limited. An earlier systematic review carrying the same registration number, also of 71 studies, gave the dose range as 16.8 mg to 17.5 g a day, rated 12 of those studies as relatively high quality (a Jadad score of 3 or more) and gave nausea, stomach ache and diarrhoea as examples of the gastrointestinal symptoms. A review of lysine supplementation for growth in children and adolescents described the supplements as generally considered clinically safe, with side effects limited to subjective gastrointestinal symptoms, but cautioned that excessive intake can lead to an imbalance of amino acids, and called for further research on safety. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
